Lecturer: Mihir Tandon; scribe: Terry Qiu.

Last week, we load-balanced across multiple robots by reducing to the tree-cover problem, for which we derived a 4-approx.
We continue this trend of multiple-robots by another decomposition of the grid, this time into rectangles.
Namely, how to cut a rectilinear polygon into rectangles minimizing an affine objective function:

- **input**: a rectilinear polygon $P$ and costs $\alpha, \beta \ge 0$
- **output**: rectangles $S_1, \ldots, S_n$ with $\bigcup_i S_i = P$, minimizing $\sum_i (\alpha + \beta \cdot A(S_i))$

See [full notes](/files/notes/fa26-cgshop/11-12/notes.pdf).
